artifacts.summary: Records that deliverable (a) (a hand-added actions/cache step) was deliberately not implemented, confirmed by live CI run log and cache-store evidence that lean-action@v1's default-on cache already covers .lake/build; lands deliverable (b) (timeout-minutes: 300 parity on ci.yml's build job); amends docs/development/CI_CD_PROCESS.md's GitHub Actions Cache subsection with the three facts it omitted; corrects a stale lean_exe count comment in lakefile.toml; and names the per-job cache-save-boundary gap as a follow-up candidate.

completion_data.completion_summary: Added timeout-minutes: 300 to ci.yml's build job for parity with docs.yml; amended CI_CD_PROCESS.md's existing GitHub Actions Cache section with the lean-action provenance, per-job save boundary, and live re-verification pointers (confirmed against a real completed run and the live cache store); corrected a stale lean_exe count comment in lakefile.toml. Deliberately did not add a second actions/cache step, since lean-action@v1 already caches .lake/build by default.

memory_candidates.content: When a task's filed ACCEPTANCE criterion names a CI cache-restore behavior, re-verify it against LIVE state at implementation time (a completed run's log via `gh run view <id> --log | grep -i cache`, plus `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/caches` for the live cache store), not only against a research-time log inspection carried forward. In this repository, `leanprover/lean-action@v1`'s own composite `actions/cache/restore`/`actions/cache/save` steps (triggered by its `use-github-cache` input, default true) already cache the whole `.lake` directory per job -- a project adding its own separate `actions/cache` step on the same path would duplicate upload/compression cost and quota for no coverage gain. The one real, measured limitation: the save half runs inside that single composite step, so any `lake build` invocation placed AFTER it in the same CI job writes into `.lake/build` after the snapshot and is never persisted across runs.

When a dispatch's Batch Gate Deferral directive supersedes a plan phase's own literal verification task text (e.g. a plan task naming an unscoped `verify-deploy.sh` sweep while the dispatch says to discharge the phase's `full` tier against a scoped narrowing invocation instead), record the supersession explicitly as a Plan Deviation (type: altered) in both the plan's checklist annotation and the implementation summary, rather than silently swapping the check performed. This keeps the deviation discoverable from the plan file alone even if the dispatch-level directive is not re-read later.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic CI .lake/build caching
sapience_notes.value: leanprover/lean-action@v1's use-github-cache input defaults to true and its composite actions/cache/restore + actions/cache/save steps cache the entire .lake directory (not just Mathlib oleans) per job, keyed on OS+arch+lake-manifest.json+toolchain+commit-sha with a sha-less fallback key. There is no separate actions/cache step in any of this repo's three workflow files, and that absence is not evidence caching is off -- confirmed live: run 44420618072 logged a cache hit (~2.6 GB restored), and the repo's Actions cache store held 4 live lake-Linux-X64-... entries.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic CI cache per-job save boundary
sapience_notes.value: lean-action@v1's actions/cache/save runs inside its own single composite step, before ci.yml's later Compile lean_exe roots loop (15 targets) and the lake build BimodalTools/BimodalToolsTest --wfail steps. Those later builds' .lake/build output is written after the snapshot and is never persisted, so they re-elaborate from scratch on every CI run even though the main lean-action build step itself is cached. Closing this requires use-github-cache: false plus a hand-rolled job-wide restore/save pair, deliberately deferred pending a before/after timing measurement.

sapience_notes.subject: Task 829 deliverable (a) reversal
sapience_notes.value: The task was filed demanding an actions/cache step for .lake/build on the premise that no caching existed. Live evidence refuted this premise at both research and implementation time: the project's lean-action@v1 invocation already caches .lake/build by default. The correct implementation response was to NOT add a redundant cache step, and instead document the existing mechanism (which the repo's own CI docs had only partially described) so future contributors grepping for actions/cache do not re-derive the same wrong conclusion.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic repo tooling defect: suite-selection-map.data preflight
sapience_notes.value: .claude/scripts/tests/suite-selection-map.data line 37 names test-verification-scope-lib.sh as the test suite for scripts/lib/verification-scope-lib.sh, but that test file does not exist yet (a self-referential new-library-suite entry documented in the data file's own comment as 'added in a later phase of the record that created it', which has apparently not landed). This causes verify-touched.sh to fail at preflight with exit 2 for ANY touched-path set, unrelated to the actual files being checked -- observed repeatedly on 2026-11-19 across three separate invocations in task 829's implement phase.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic repo: lean_exe target count
sapience_notes.value: lakefile.toml declares 15 [[lean_exe]] targets (grep -c '^\[\[lean_exe\]\]' and scripts/lake_targets.py exe-roots both agree), not 13 as a stale comment on the BimodalTools lean_lib claimed before this task corrected it.
